en: Title: Suprabhātastava Author: Harṣa Source: Liu 2022
Tibetan: D 1167 oṃ namo buddhāya || English: Oṃ, homage to the Buddha!
Though he has been praised with hymns of praise by the hosts of gods, the leaders of the Siddhas and Gandharvas, and by eminent ascetics in both heaven and on earth,
I too, despite my feeble power, offer praise to the Noble Fully Awakened One.
When Garuḍa has flown into the sky, why do the bees not follow? || 1 ||
O Victor, in this world shrouded by the dense darkness of night of all the clouds of afflictions, you have awakened through the attainment of instantaneous knowledge; thus,
you are perfectly enlightened like a lotus at the end of the night.
I shall entreat [Thee] with devotion through these clusters of flowers of praise. || 2 ||
He who has destroyed the faction of evil, whose defects are entirely exhausted, whose complexion is like molten gold, whose eyes are as long as full-blown lotuses,
who possesses a most beautiful halo, and who is endowed with the splendor of a radiant circle of light.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 3 ||
To the conqueror of the power of Māra, the destroyer of the Kāpotī [heretical] sect, the benefactor of the three worlds, the remover of the thicket of the creeper of womanhood,
the knower of the supreme bliss of tranquility, and the breaker of the mountain of ignorance—
O Ten-Powered One, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 4 ||
The Buddha, the first-born among asuras, gods, and men, the sustainer of all worlds, the sole name for the creation of the universe,
with eyes as broad as lotus petals, now sleeps in the world.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 5 ||
Though standing upon the slope of the eastern mountain, copper-red like a slice of coral, the destroyer of the mass of darkness, and the sole eye of all people—
the sun too has now entirely fallen asleep, as if intoxicated with passion.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak.
Even that moon, white as the tusk of an elephant, cool-rayed,
the mark upon the night like a tilaka, and the crest-jewel of Śiva—
having not yet lost the glow of its intoxication, has also fallen asleep.
O Ten-Powered One, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 7 ||
Even that Creator, the lotus-born one, who possesses four excellent arms, eight faces (four times two),
who knows the rules and procedures for recitation, who is the expounder of the Sāmaveda,
and who is stainless— has fallen asleep.
O Ten-Powered One, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 8 ||
Blue as the petal of a water-lily, with eyes as broad as white lotuses, the slayer of the hosts of the enemies of the gods, the creator of the universe, possessing universal form—
even Hari himself has long been asleep, not yet released from dwelling in the womb.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at the break of day. || 9 ||
Resembling the peak of the Snowy Mountain, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread, skilled in the burning of the three cities, and clad in an upper garment of tiger skin,
he who bears the trident sleeps eternally together with the daughter of the foremost of mountains.
O Ten-Powered One, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 10 ||
Paśupati, with his mass of matted hair tawny like a Kapila cow, his eyes copper-red and glowing, uniquely skilled in severing attachments even at an untimely hour—
though his own body was pierced by the arrows of Smara, he too lay as if asleep amidst the sacrificial fire.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 11 ||
Even the Lord of the Gods, though holding a blazing thunderbolt in his hand and being difficult for the Dānavas to conquer, had his mind deluded by the charms of Śacī;
he slept day and night, submerged in the mire of passion.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 12 ||
Resembling the snow-white moon-lotus, with eyes reddened from drinking wine,
his limbs firm and hard, his hand grasping a plow—
here lies Balarāma, long asleep, his neck entwined around Revatī.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 13 ||
The elephant-faced one, the sole possessor of tusks, the creator of obstacles everywhere, with the ichor of rut flowing from him and his temples resonant with the humming of bees—
even Gaṇapati himself was asleep, intoxicated by the drinking of wine.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 14 ||
That six-faced son of the Three-eyed One, who is blue like the Atasī flower, whose spear-tip is tipped with fresh gold, and who is the slayer of Krauñca—
that Kumāra too lies fast asleep.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 15 ||
Yama, Varuṇa, and Kubera; the lords of the Yakṣas, Daityas, and Uragas;
the world-protectors in heaven, on earth, and in the sky, as well as others—even they were overcome by sleep when gazed upon by the intoxicating sidelong glances of the young women.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 16 ||
O sages, here are the great ones— Vatsa, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Adri, Kratu, Pulaha, Vasiṣṭha, Vyāsa, Vālmīki, and Gārgya;
yet even they are perpetually fast asleep, attached to the hips of young women.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 17 ||
Submerged in the ocean of existence, their bodies shrouded by the net of delusion—
Manu, Kapila, Kaṇāda, and others whose minds are bewildered;
devoid of the bliss of tranquility, those fools are likewise asleep.
O Ten-Powered One, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak.
Deprived of food and clothing, devoted to the yoga of death, beset by many various calamities, their bodies burnt like those of hungry ghosts (pretas),
and deprived of both [human and divine] destinies— even they are naked and fast asleep.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 18 ||
O Lord, whatever small portion of virtue has arisen in me through my devotion by praising Your qualities— purified by the splendor of its true intent— may that,
in this world, swiftly destroy all subsequent rebirths.
O Daśabala, may there always be a beautiful dawn for you at daybreak. || 19 ||
A beautiful dawn belongs to you alone, whose eye is opened by wisdom;
for those blinded by the darkness of ignorance, the sun has forever set. (20)
Again there is dawn, again the sun has risen, again the moon, and again the night;
likewise, death, old age, and birth occur yet once more.
One of deluded intellect does not perceive the coming and going [of the breath]. || 21 ||
While the world sleeps in the darkness of the night of ignorance, upon the vast bed of craving with sense-objects as its pillow,
and rolls about amidst the fruits of good and evil deeds;
Salutations to him who is ever awake. || 22 ||
A beautiful dawn, a favorable star, greeted by prosperity;
day after day I bow to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. (23)
At sacred fords, hundreds of herds of cows drink the water and reach satisfaction, yet it does not undergo depletion;
even so is it with the sage who is praised by the best of poets.
The treasury of virtues of this ocean of qualities is never exhausted.

Having praised the Teacher of the World, the supreme Great Sage— the ocean of merit of the True Dharma, free from duality, whose darkness of passion and hatred has been destroyed, whose senses are tranquil, and who is desireless—
whatever vast merit I have thereby acquired, by that may the entire world quickly [attain enlightenment].
When the Daśabala is gladdened by the hymn of praise at dawn, may they attain supreme faith. || 25 ||
The Suprabhātastava is completed. This work is the composition of King Śrī Harṣa.
